answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on a bonded identity cost. Each new agent must lock up a quartz-backed stake that is forfeited if its answers are judged fraudulent, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means tying up a thousand stakes. Peers then attest only answers from accounts that have a clean history over many epochs, which timber-thick track records make expensive to fake. A ledge of minimum age before rewards unlock adds time cost on top of money cost.
